_WHAT_THIS_IS: The record of WHICH on-chain verifier the checked-in client prover blob is allowed to talk to.
packages/stark-prover/wasm/p01_stark_bg.wasm and its four inlined twins are the prover every
client actually runs. The proof wire format is agreed with the on-chain verifier and NOTHING on
the wire declares which generation produced a proof. A client that is one generation ahead of the
deployed program does not fail to build, does not fail to parse and does not fail early: it fails
at the very END of a long chunked proof upload, on chain, with FriFoldCheckFailed. That reads as an
unexplained transaction failure, which is why this file exists.
scripts/deployed-verifier-check.mjs compares the checked-in blob against this record and fails the
build when they are not compatible. It is wired into the client build and publish steps, not only CI.
_HOW_TO_MAKE_THE_GATE_GREEN: There is exactly ONE legitimate way, and it is not an edit to this file:
1. Deploy the CURRENT programs/p01_stark_verifier to the cluster named below.
2. Re-measure this record from the chain:
node packages/stark-prover/scripts/deployed-verifier-check.mjs --measure
That prints a fresh `deployed` block read straight off the programdata account.
3. Paste the measured block in, and set deployed.accepts_client_blob_sha256 to the sha256 of the
blob you proved against that deployment.
4. Re-run the gate with the on-chain leg:
node packages/stark-prover/scripts/deployed-verifier-check.mjs --verify-onchain
EDITING deployed.proof_format_generation OR deployed.accepts_client_blob_sha256 WITHOUT REDEPLOYING
IS THE FAILURE MODE THIS FILE EXISTS TO PREVENT. It makes the offline gate green and every proof
still fails on chain. --verify-onchain catches exactly that: it refetches the programdata account,
recomputes deployed.elf_sha256, and re-derives the generation from the deployed bytes. A record that
claims a generation the chain does not have is rejected against the chain, and no edit to this file
can change what the chain returns.
The other direction is also blocked. Reverting the client blob to the older generation to match the
chain makes THIS gate green, but packages/stark-prover/src/wireFormat.test.ts then goes red on all
seven per-circuit sha256 digests, because the blob no longer matches the Rust prover in this tree.
The two gates constrain each other; neither alone is sufficient.
The marker strings the gate scans for are HARDCODED in deployed-verifier-check.mjs, not read from
this file, so weakening the evidence blocks below cannot weaken the scan. They are reproduced here
for a human reader.
_WHICH_EXISTING_GATES_LET_A_STALE_BLOB_T: Both of the WASM gates that existed before this file compare the blob against THIS TREE. Neither
one has ever looked at the chain, and both are GREEN right now while every proof this blob produces
scripts/stark-wasm-twins.mjs --check   proves the five artifacts carry the same bytes as each
other. Says nothing about the deployed program.

equal what the Rust prover in stark/ emits. That is the
SAME side of the skew. If the tree is ahead of the chain,
this gate confirms the tree agrees with itself and passes.
src/wasmProbeScan.test.ts              proves no fails-closed probe identifier survives in the
Nothing else in the repo compares a client artifact to a deployed program.
programs/p01_stark_verifier/tests/cu_budget.rs builds its own .so locally and never reads the chain.

generation_evidence.method: byte scan of the deployed ELF for msg! format-string literals that B1 introduced in programs/p01_stark_verifier/src/verify.rs, controlled by sibling literals from the same file that predate B1
generation_evidence.reading: The B1 degree-bound msg! at verify.rs:1032 is absent while five sibling msg! literals from the same file are present, so the scan is working and the deployed bytes simply predate check_final_poly_degree_bound. `deep-v1` is the DEEP_COEFF_TAG byte string at verify.rs:962; its absence is corroborating but weaker, because an 8-byte byte-string literal can be materialised inline rather than kept in rodata.
generation_evidence.the_gap_is_wider_than_b1: Also absent from the deployed ELF: the C6 merkle_update boundary tag bnd-c6 (verify.rs:2592) and `verify_uniform: probed circuit ` (lib.rs:470, landed in commit 4bc69cb4). The deployment is several generations behind HEAD, not one. Redeploying fixes all of them at once; this record only tracks the B1 boundary because that is the one that silently breaks every proof.
